$comment: The Kp lookup exists four times — src/services/noaaApi.ts (getKpIndex), ios/App/StormWidget/KpSource.swift, android/app/src/main/java/com/stormwatcher/app/widget/KpSource.kt and supabase/functions/send-kp-alerts/index.ts (fetchCurrentKp). They cannot share code across TS/Swift/Kotlin/Deno, so they share this instead. src/services/kpContract.test.ts asserts the TypeScript one matches; the other three are checked by hand against this file. Both drifts found on 2026-08-06 would have been caught by reading it.

primary.name: GFZ Potsdam
primary.pick: last element whose Kp is a number >= 0
primary.$comment: Trailing bins are null until GFZ publishes the period. Never substitute 0 — Kp 0.0 is a real ultra-quiet reading, so a fabricated 0 is indistinguishable from a genuine one and silently suppresses storm alerts.

fallback.name: NOAA SWPC
fallback.$comment: kp_index is the 3-hour bin — the same quantity GFZ publishes. estimated_kp is a per-minute estimate that swings between bins (0.33 -> 0.67 -> 0.33 while the bin holds 0.333), so reading it first puts a different number on each surface.

$comment2: -1 means 'no data'. 0.0 is real data. Freshness, never the value, decides whether a cached Kp is usable.
